thread:
Anya (ML): Quick follow-up to the RFC: proposing we split quant artifacts into two distinct things: a rich Profile (offline, evaluative) and a tiny Contract (runtime, hot-path). Wanted to lay out tradeoffs before we freeze schema.

Raj (Runtime): 👍 split makes sense. Main runtime constraints: evaluate Contract in <50ns per request, tiny memory, backward-parseable. How small are we talking?

Anya (ML): Contract should be <1KB ideally. Minimal fields: contract_version, allowed_bitwidths, priority_list (models), per_request_thresholds (tiny floats), hysteresis_ms. Everything else stays in Profile.

Morgan (Ops): Ops checklist: semantic version in Contract + checksum. Rollouts: if Contract incompatible we must fail closed to safest model and emit alert. Can we make parser tolerant to unknown fields?

Raj (Runtime): Parser will ignore unknown keys and fallback on defaults. Example compact Contract:
```json
{"cv":"1","bw":[8,4],"min_ppl_increase":0.1,"fallback":"redwood-3b-int8-safe","hysteresis":150}
```
No nested maps. Keep names short to save bytes.

Kai (Research): From eval side, Profile contains the heavy stuff: per-layer sensitivity, slice-specific regressions (e.g., code/math), and recommended quantization knobs. Profile example (offline):
```json
{"model":"redwood-3b","commit":"c0ffee","per_layer": [{"l":0,"ppl_drop":0.02}],"slices":["code","qa"],"recommended":"fp8","notes":"headwise issues >1024"}
```
Profiles live in model-metadata and are versioned.

Sam (Platform): Two platform concerns: (1) where Contracts are stored and cached by runtime nodes, (2) invalidation strategy when Profile -> Contract is regenerated. Ops needs a deterministic key for cache ttl.

Anya (ML): We can derive Contract key = model:commit:contract_v:sha256(contract). Profile includes eval_id so we know provenance.

Morgan (Ops): For rollout semantics: staging -> canary -> global. Contract change should add a field 'min_runtime_version' so old nodes gracefully ignore new constructs. Also include 'rollback_signal' URL for one-click ops.

Raj (Runtime): We'll add a thrift-light loader that keeps Contracts in shared memory and hot-reloads on change. Need to ensure atomic swap of contract blob. Also suggest a small feature-flag to disable Contracts per-customer for debugging.

Anya (ML): Good. Another tradeoff: expressiveness vs simplicity. We can't encode complex policies (per-prompt regex hooks) in Contract without inflating size. My suggestion: leave complex policy hooks to Profile + offloaded policy service; Contract only contains numeric thresholds and IDs referencing policy templates.

Kai (Research): Agree. We should include a small 'policy_ref' string (template id) rather than embedding logic. Runtime can call policy service asynchronously if needed, but default to conservative behavior if policy service unreachable.

Raj (Runtime): Telemetry: runtime must emit reason codes for every quant decision: ACCEPT_CONTRACT, FALLBACK_HYSTERESIS, POLICY_SERVICE_ERR. Keep reason codes as short strings. That helps debug quality regressions.

Morgan (Ops): Also: include canary gating metrics: token_p95_latency, quality_regressions(count), cost_delta. Ops will abort rollout if any quality_regressions > threshold. How do we map profile-specified quality tests into runtime checks?

Anya (ML): Profiles will list a small set of sentinel prompts and expected metrics; the rollout service will run them during canary and compare. Not on every request.

Sam (Platform): Implementation notes:
- Contract store = S3 + Dynamo index for latest per model:commit
- Runtime caches in shared memory + SIGHUP-style reload from local journal
- Canary controller compares telemetry and sentinel tests

Raj (Runtime): Microperf benchmark I ran: parsing a 300B JSON took ~1.2us; our compact Contract parse (short keys) is <120ns. So size + key lengths matter. Also GC pressure if we allocate per-request — must reuse object instances.

Kai (Research): Ops question on per-tenant overrides: should Contracts allow tenant-specific relaxations? e.g., enterprise opts into int4 even if global Contract disallows it.

Morgan (Ops): We want per-tenant overrides but behind RBAC and audit logs. Suggest 'overrides_allowed': true/false and require signed override tokens. That keeps runtime simple: if override token present and allowed, accept extra bitwidths.

Anya (ML): Good addition. Also propose 'safety_score_floor' float to force fallback if runtime confidence drops below. Keeps quality guardrails.

Raj (Runtime): Putting it together: final Contract schema v1 (compact):
```json
{
  "cv":"1",
  "bw":[8,4],
  "fallback":"redwood-3b-int8-safe",
  "min_ppl_inc":0.08,
  "hysteresis_ms":150,
  "policy_ref":"pfl-001",
  "overrides_allowed":false,
  "safety_floor":0.65
}
```
Runtime will map keys: bw->allowed_bitwidths, min_ppl_inc->min_ppl_increase, safety_floor->prob_floor. Short keys to save cycles.

Sam (Platform): Can we keep a migration guide mapping long names -> short keys for readability in the model-metadata UI? Humans shouldn't deal with the minified format.

Anya (ML): We'll keep Profiles human-readable; Contracts generated from Profiles by the optimizer/minifier. UI shows expanded view and the raw compact blob.

deploy-bot: deploy started for branch quant-contracts/v1 at 1748510000

Raj (Runtime): Once deploy is up, I'll run microbenchmarks and post numbers. Also will add reason codes to logs.

Morgan (Ops): I'll draft the canary abort thresholds and rollback playbook (including how to revoke tenant overrides).

Kai (Research): I'll add eval pipeline changes so Profiles emit the recommended contract and eval_id.

Anya (ML): Thanks team. Next steps: Sam write storage design doc, Raj bench and PR, Morgan prepare ops playbook, Kai wire eval->profile output. Sync in 48h. :thumbsup:
